event.name: Write The Docs Kenya Conference 2026
event.theme: The Future of Documentation: AI, Open Source, and Building Better Developer Experiences

speakers.name: Alias Nutcase
speakers.bio: I just build stuffs and enjoy my life
topics: Code is Cheap, Context is Expensive: Docs that Survive the FinTech Fire

speakers.name: Bethwel Kiplagat
speakers.tagline: Software Engineer, Technical Co-founder at Crezine Cashdoor, and documentation believer
speakers.bio:
Bethwel Kiplagat is a Software Engineer and Technical Co-founder at Crezine Cashdoor, where he builds user-friendly applications and manages the technical side of a growing startup. With a background in Computer Science, he discovered early that great code alone isn't enough — users need clear, kind, and useful documentation to truly benefit from any product.

This belief in clarity and empowerment drives everything he does: as a universal mentor at the GeeKulcha Student Society (GKSS), he helps new developers navigate technical documentation without getting lost. He also contributes to open-source projects, often focusing on improving READMEs and contributor guides.

Bethwel is applying to speak at Write The Docs Kenya because he wants to share what he's learned about documentation best practices — from his own early confusion to the small, repeatable habits that now make his docs more useful. This will be his first conference talk, and he's excited to learn from and contribute to the WTD community.
topics: The 5-Minute README Fix: Small Changes, Big Impact

speakers.name: Bret Oreta
speakers.bio: I’m a software developer and systems builder focused on creating scalable web applications, automation workflows, and developer-focused tools. My work spans full-sack web development, AI-assisted workflows, API integrations, and knowledge systems designed to improve developer experience and operational efficiency. I’ve worked on projects involving automation platforms, vector databases, internal support systems, payment integrations, and AI-powered retrieval workflows that help teams turn scattered documentation into accessible, searchable knowledge. I’m particularly interested in the intersection of developer experience, documentation, and practical AI applications for modern engineering teams.
topics: From Dead Docs to Searchable Knowledge

speakers.name: Caleb Jephuneh
speakers.bio:
I am a tech entrepreneur with two successful exits, driven by a relentless passion for building impactful technology. With over seven years of hands-on experience in software engineering, I have worked across innovative startups, large enterprises, and award-winning agencies, building a strong foundation in both software and AI.

As a global AI speaker, I focus on inspiring the next generation of innovators to think beyond limitations and challenge conventional approaches to technology. I am passionate about empowering young innovators to think out of the box, build boldly, and create solutions that drive real-world impact.

In 2025, I was honored with the Young Africa CEO of the Year award by the CIO 100 Awards, and my company was recognized as one of the fastest-growing companies in Africa—milestones that reflect both my entrepreneurial journey and commitment to innovation.

I am dedicated to shaping the future of technology in Africa and beyond by fostering creativity, pushing boundaries, and turning ideas into scalable impact.
topics: Multilingual docs without losing your mind (or your meaning)

speakers.name: Daisy Auma
speakers.tagline: Developer Relations Engineer, Co - founder Lux Academy,WTM Ambassador
speakers.bio: Daisy Auma is a Developer Relations Engineer and technical writer who most recently led documentation for Archetype AI's Newton physical AI platform. She co-founded LuxDevHQ, an AI and data science bootcamp now training 2,400+ students across 16 African countries, and is pursuing an MSc in Data Science at the University of East London. Her background spans developer advocacy and API documentation at Cloudflare, Kudan, and Safaricom (M-PESA Daraja). She is a Women Techmakers Ambassador and Google Community Builder, and creates educational tech content as @daisy_codes.
topics: Documenting an AI That Sees the Physical World: Building a CI/CD Pipeline for Foundation Model Docs

speakers.name: Derdus Kenga
speakers.bio: 6 years of technical writing experience, 8 years of university teaching Experience, 2 years of software engineering experience, 1 year vibe coding.
topics: Understand LLMs and RAG basics to write better product content

speakers.name: Ephraim Mwereza
speakers.bio:
Ephraim Mwereza is a technology leader and innovator harnessing the power of software and AI to drive transformative change across Africa. 

He builds localized, sustainable digital solutions that address critical challenges in health, education, and inclusivity, ensuring even the most vulnerable communities benefit from the tech revolution. 

Combining deep technical expertise with a human-centered, ethical approach, Ephraim seeks collaborations with leading experts to maximize impact and build a brighter, more inclusive future.
topics: From App Engine to Cloud Run: A Docker Migration Story

speakers.name: Felix Jumason
speakers.bio: Building cool software in Telco industry
topics: How Cursor Uses Documentation to Build Better AI Coding Workflows

speakers.name: Hidaya Vanessa
speakers.bio: Software developer and techie passionate about simplifying APIs and developer tools for beginners
topics: The Docs We Don't Call Documentation

speakers.name: Himesh Siriwardana
speakers.bio:
Himesh Siriwardana is a technical writer specializing in Identity and Access Management documentation. He works on documentation strategy, content architecture, developer-focused content, and documentation workflows for complex security products.

As the content owner for IAM documentation, Himesh collaborates with engineering, product, developer relations, customer success, and support teams to create user-focused documentation experiences. His work focuses on turning complex identity and security concepts into practical content that helps developers, administrators, and enterprise customers adopt products with confidence.

He is especially interested in documentation systems and the evolving role of technical writers as content strategists and documentation architects.
topics: My Engineering Team Is My Documentation Team

speakers.name: Jimmy Tron
speakers.bio:
I am a community manager at SpaceYaTech and also work in tech. 
I specialize in backend web development using Django. With extensive experience in Linux systems, administrative tools on both Windows and Linux, web hosting and services, robotics, IoT, and Git/GitHub, I have worked on various projects.
topics: Tailoring Open source contribution for career transitions

speakers.name: Job Alex Muturi
speakers.bio: Software engineer, DevRel & DevEx Engineer, and builder focused on developer tooling, executable documentation, and technical storytelling workflows. Creator of slides-tape, a Markdown-first orchestration engine for automated demos, re-playable tutorials, and executable developer experiences and DatabridgeCLI, a database compiler that turns databases + intent into deterministic, production-ready APIs, SDKs, and contracts — with no runtime lock-in.
topics: From Static Docs to Executables: Building Replayable and Verifiable Documentation Workflows

speakers.name: Leen Kirau Noted
speakers.tagline: Community Development Advocate & Digital Literacy Strategist
speakers.bio: Leen Kirau is a community development practitioner and student leader at Alupe University, deeply committed to bridging the digital divide through grassroots education and peer advocacy. With strong experience in youth mobilization, digital literacy initiatives, and strategic AI frameworks, she focuses on making emerging technologies accessible, inclusive, and actionable for local communities.
topics: Cultivating AI Literacy: Making Tech Documentation Inclusive for All Communities

speakers.name: Mosongo Danfold
speakers.tagline: TECH POLICY ADVOCATE|CYBER SECURITY & FORENSICS .ENG| TECH WRITER
speakers.bio: Mosongo Danfold is a Tech Policy Advocate , Cybersecurity and Forensics Engineer. He is the founder of TECH.PATHS, an initiative that equips African youth with digital literacy and mentorship on Tech sovereignty. Recognised as a tech diplomat and statesman, he works at the intersection of cybersecurity, policy, and youth empowerment, contributing to national digital governance processes and speaking on digital sovereignty and ethical technology.
topics: The APT Approach to Documentation: Consistency Over CV Padding

speakers.name: Prince Onyeanuna
speakers.bio:
Prince Onyeanuna is a dedicated technical writer at Pi Squared, with a strong foundation in cloud-native technologies and DevOps engineering.

He has contributed extensively to open-source projects, notably with OpenMRS, where he honed his skills in crafting comprehensive technical documentation.

Prince's passion for technology and education is evident in his mentorship roles within the Technical Writers Mentorship Program open-source community, where he has guided numerous aspiring writers.
topics: Navigating Documentation Challenges: Success Stories from the OpenMRS Wiki Revamp Project

speakers.name: Samuel Macharia
speakers.tagline: Google Developer Expert for Google Cloud | Cloud DevOps Engineer
speakers.bio:
Samuel Macharia is a skilled Cloud DevOps Engineer with a passion for leveraging cloud technologies i.e. AWS, Azure & Google Cloud to drive innovation. He holds certifications as a Google Cloud Certified Professional Cloud Architect and Microsoft Certified DevOps Engineer Expert, equipping him to design and manage secure, scalable, and high-performing infrastructure across multi-cloud environments.

Samuel is dedicated to empowering the next generation of tech talent and has served as a mentor in the Grow Your Skills for Sub-Saharan Africa Google Cloud Program 2024. With a focus on practical solutions and a commitment to communities including AWS User Group Kenya, CloudForce Sky, GDG Eldoret & Write the Docs Kenya where he volunteers, Samuel is excited to share his knowledge and inspire others to embrace the power of the cloud.

Coming from a community best known for resilience and entrepreneurial spirit, he opted to code his own path forward. When he's not building in tech, he's exploring new creative endeavors, mastering chess strategies, or immersed in an intense crime drama.
topics: From App Engine to Cloud Run: A Docker Migration Story

speakers.name: Sandra Kimiring
speakers.bio:
I build AI and machine learning systems end-to-end - from raw data and modeling to deployment and backend infrastructure.

Currently, I’m a Co-Founder at Inua360, where we’re building AI-powered business intelligence tools for SMEs, and I also contribute to AI system design and implementation work at Uamuzi Foundation.
topics: Beyond the Notebook: Architecting Organizational Memory for ML Teams

speakers.name: Stanley Ndagi
speakers.bio:
Stanley brings expertise in leadership, technical product and program management, full-stack cross-platform software engineering, AI adoption and tooling, and comprehensive technical communication. He empowers teams, steers technical products and programs, engineers versatile software solutions, and effectively bridges the gap between technical complexities and clear understanding for various stakeholders.

He is experienced in working remotely in distributed, multidisciplinary, cross-cultural, and multinational teams. His work cuts across fintech, agriculture, government, fashion, not-for-profit, and education sectors.

He delivers value, builds team capacity, generates revenue, optimizes processes, and reduces costs. Technical writing is another forte, covering content strategy and design, and information architecture, while also enhancing developer education, experience, and productivity. A champion of free and open-source code, Stanley is well versed in Agile-Scrum methodology.

Stanley leads TechKln, a community championing digital literacy, and mentors professionals globally through ADPList, where he has been recognized as a Top Achiever. He has also been recognized as a GitHub Star and CircleCI Champion.

After hours and off work, Stanley enjoys quality time with his family, engages with individuals and organizational teams from early-stage startups to 60+ year-old institutions across SDLC stages, and tinkers with hardware and software projects spanning IoT, carpentry, and mechanics.
topics: Docs in the Real World: Platforms, AI, and the Cost of Getting It Right

speakers.name: Tonny Gidraph
speakers.tagline: Netmatta | Technical Writer & Software Developer | Turning complexity into clarity
speakers.bio:
Tonny Gidraph is a technical writer and software developer with experience creating technical content across software development, Raspberry Pi projects, Linux systems, cybersecurity, web development, and emerging technologies. He focuses on translating complex technical concepts into practical, easy-to-follow content for diverse audiences.

With a hands-on background in building and experimenting with technology, Tonny combines technical knowledge with clear communication to create documentation that is accessible to different audiences.

He is particularly interested in how AI is transforming the documentation process and how technical writers can adapt to new tools while maintaining accuracy, usability, and trust.

Portfolio: https://tonnygidraph.vercel.app
topics: AI Won’t Replace Technical Writers - It’s Changing How We Work

speakers.name: Zawadi Mukuru
speakers.tagline: Full stack Data Scientist,Machine Learning Engineer
speakers.bio:
I am a data scientist and machine learning engineer currently pursuing Data Science and Analytics at JKUAT. I specialize in building and deploying end-to-end machine learning systems, with a focus on applied AI, data engineering, and production-grade model development.

My work spans the full machine learning lifecycle—from data pipelines and feature engineering to model training, evaluation, and deployment in real-world environments. I have experience designing scalable systems such as recommendation engines, predictive models, and intelligent data-driven platforms that operate under practical constraints.

I am particularly interested in how machine learning systems are built to function reliably in production, especially in environments where data is noisy, requirements evolve quickly, and systems must remain maintainable over time. I work primarily with Python, SQL, and modern ML frameworks to turn complex data into robust, deployable intelligence.
topics: Beyond the Notebook: Architecting Organizational Memory for ML Teams
